interactions.summary: A student asks whether souls in heaven also have these fields, and Jiang answers that the fields ultimately bend away from bodily form and back into divine unity.
The class presses on whether gluttony’s hunger is real or metaphorical, and Jiang insists it is spiritually real hunger rather than merely symbolic appetite.

claims.claim: Jiang says heavenly souls no longer keep a body-fitted shade because their fields have returned home and bent themselves to the divine light.
On earth hunger is physical, but in purgatory the same pattern becomes a soul-level process of longing and restraint.
Jiang insists that purgatorial hunger must be real rather than merely metaphorical, otherwise the pain and desire would have no meaning.
His final picture is two-dimensional: body and soul are combined on earth, but after death the body can vanish while the soul retains bodily semblance in a spiritual mode.

signature_moments.moment: The fields stop fitting the human body and start fitting heaven itself.
signature_moments.source_phrase: they now bend to fit the divine light
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is Jiang’s clearest image for de-individuated beatitude after the shade-stage.

signature_moments.moment: Hunger after death is declared spiritually real rather than symbolically decorative.
signature_moments.source_phrase: only if it's real, does it have any meaning
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This defends the seriousness of purgatorial suffering against reduction to metaphor.

chronology_notes.note: This packet extends the June 26 morphic-field model by distinguishing shade-form, heavenly reintegration, and spiritual hunger.
